fields.quote: Retry only retryable failures, within a fixed budget
fields.rationale: after throws when !error.retryable or attempt === retries, so only retryable send failures are retried and only while attempt < retries. The loop bound is the retries argument (source contract: nonnegative integer; separate calls share no retry counter). Probe after.permanent.calls is 1; after.exhausted.calls is 3 when retries is 2.
source.json title begins with 'Cedar Relay: filter retries and increase delays'.

fields.quote: Permanent failures stop immediately; retryable failures use increasing requested delays without a delivery deduplication guarantee.
fields.rationale: after throws on !error.retryable before sleep; probe after.permanent is calls 1, delays [], error 'permanent'. Retryable path uses sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt); probe after.exhausted.delays is [10, 20]. Contract: delays are requested milliseconds, not wall-clock; no deduplication or idempotency contract. Probe after.duplicate.effects is 2.

probe.mjs logs assumptions: 'Deterministic modeled send outcomes and immediate sleep promises; no timing or production measurement.' probe-results.json repeats that string. The line describes the supplied evidence method, not a program guarantee.

fields.quote: A rejected acknowledgment can still follow a committed remote effect.
fields.rationale: Contract: a send rejection may happen after the remote side effect commits. Probe duplicate outcomes are [{ effect: true, error: transient }, { effect: true }]; after.duplicate.effects is 2 with result 'delivered'. Probe comment: 'a lost acknowledgment permits duplicate side effects'.
Chapter label only. It does not assert program behavior.

fields.quote: The old loop retried every rejection
fields.rationale: before retries send rejections until attempt === retries (probe before.permanent.calls is 2 after a permanent send error). It does not retry every rejection: await sleep(10) has no local catch, and the contract says sleep rejection propagates. Probe before.sleepFailure is calls 1, error 'sleep-failed' — the sleep rejection is not retried. Same-section body narrows this to rejected sends.

fields.quote: The old loop retried rejected sends until the retry budget ran out. It requested a ten-millisecond delay between attempts.
fields.rationale: before catch retries any send error unless attempt === retries, then await sleep(10). Probe before.exhausted is calls 3, delays [10, 10], error 'transient'. before.permanent sleeps 10 once then a later send can still return 'delivered'. Contract: delays are requested milliseconds.
Chapter label only. It does not assert program behavior.
after inspects error.retryable and attempt === retries in catch before await sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt). Non-retryable and final-attempt errors throw without sleep (after.permanent.delays is []).

fields.quote: The changed loop stops on a non-retryable error. With a budget of two retries, retryable failures request delays of 10 then 20 milliseconds before the final send. This permits up to three sends. A rejected sleep prevents the next send.
fields.rationale: All four sentences are scoped to after and match code plus probe: after.permanent stops at calls 1 / error 'permanent'; retries=2 yields sleep(10 * 2 ** 0) then sleep(10 * 2 ** 1) and attempt <= 2, matching after.exhausted.delays [10, 20] and calls 3; sleepFailure is calls 1 / error 'sleep-failed'. These are loop bounds and control flow, not a passing example treated as a universal delivery guarantee.
Chapter label only. It does not assert program behavior.

fields.quote: A retry can duplicate a remote effect
fields.rationale: Existential 'can' matches the contract (rejection after commit; no deduplication) and the modeled duplicate scenario: after.duplicate.effects is 2.

fields.quote: The author describes exactly-once delivery, but the supplied contract permits a send to reject after its effect commits. The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects. Separate invocations share no retry budget or exclusion mechanism.
fields.rationale: source.json body: the author says the change 'makes delivery exactly once.' Next contract sentence permits rejection after the effect commits and states no deduplication. Probe after.duplicate.effects is 2. Contract: separate calls share no retry counter and no lock or cross-call delivery exclusion. Probe after.concurrentCalls is two successful invocations with effects 1+1.
Chapter label only. It does not assert program behavior.

Comparative claim vs before, for non-retryable errors. Probe before.permanent.calls is 2 with result 'delivered'; after.permanent.calls is 1 with error 'permanent'. Retryable exhaustion still uses three sends in both (exhausted.calls is 3).

fields.quote: The change filters failures and increases requested delays. It bounds send attempts per invocation, not successful delivery or duplicate effects.
fields.rationale: after filters on error.retryable and requests 10 * 2 ** attempt vs before's constant 10 (exhausted delays [10, 10] vs [10, 20]). Loop bound is per call of after/before; contract says separate calls share no retry counter and there is no deduplication. after.duplicate.effects remains 2; concurrentCalls still sums to 2 effects.

missing_material_limitations.limitation: Requested delays are not measured wall-clock durations; probe sleeps resolve immediately.
missing_material_limitations.evidence: Contract: 'Delays are requested milliseconds, not measured wall-clock durations.' Probe assumptions: immediate sleep promises; no timing or production measurement.
missing_material_limitations.coverage: The dek and section 1 say 'requested delays' / 'request delays of 10 then 20 milliseconds' but never state that elapsed time is unmeasured. A reader can still take 10 and 20 as observed waits.

missing_material_limitations.limitation: retries is a nonnegative integer precondition; the loop does not validate other values.
missing_material_limitations.evidence: Contract: 'retries is a nonnegative integer.' Both functions use for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= retries; attempt++). Probe only uses 0 and 2.
missing_material_limitations.coverage: Unmentioned. Negative retries would skip the loop and fall through with no return value. Not modeled.

missing_material_limitations.limitation: send rejections are specified as objects with a boolean retryable property.
missing_material_limitations.evidence: Contract: 'send returns a promise and rejects with an object containing a boolean retryable property.' after reads error.retryable.
missing_material_limitations.coverage: Unmentioned. Missing retryable is falsy, so after would treat it as non-retryable and throw. Not modeled.

reviewer_language_leakage.quote: but the supplied contract permits a send to reject after its effect commits
reviewer_language_leakage.note: 'supplied contract' is review-harness diction, not reader-facing explanation of send failure.

reviewer_language_leakage.quote: The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects.
reviewer_language_leakage.note: 'modeled' and 'records two effects' echo probe.mjs (trace.effects, 'modeled send outcomes') rather than naming the failure mode for a reader.
Copies probe-results.json assumptions wording into a reader-visible metadata line.

quotes: but the supplied contract permits a send to reject after its effect commits
The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects.
reader_facing_prose.rationale: Visible copy uses harness terms (supplied contract, modeled example, recorded effects) instead of naming the send/sleep behavior for a reader. Factual density in those sentences does not make the diction reader-facing.

unresolved_uncertainty: Whether /title 'fixed budget' was meant as the retries argument per invocation (supported) or as a single shared constant across calls (contracts and concurrentCalls say there is no shared counter).
Whether /dek 'without a delivery deduplication guarantee' was meant to modify only the retryable-delay clause or the whole change; either reading is still consistent with the no-dedup contract.
Negative or non-integer retries and errors without retryable were not modeled; treating those gaps as material limitations is a judgment, not an observed contradiction.
No narration, code, or diagram fields were listed; absence of {{CODE}}/{{DIAGRAM}} entries is not an observed snippet error.

notes.examples_are_not_universal_guarantees: Section 1 states the three-send / 10-then-20 figures only with a budget of two retries, which matches attempt <= retries and 10 * 2 ** attempt. Section 2 labels two effects as a modeled example. Those are not treated here as proof of unstated universals.
notes.contradiction_vs_uncertainty: The only field-level contradiction is /sections/0/title ('every rejection') versus sleep rejection propagating without retry. Other contract gaps are listed as missing limitations or uncertainty, not as contradictions.
notes.functions_match_source: functions.mjs before/after match source.json before/after. Manifest contains no code or diagram entries.
notes.attribution: source.json body attributes both 'avoids retrying permanent failures' and 'makes delivery exactly once' to the author. The manifest attributes only the exactly-once claim to the author and treats permanent-failure filtering as the change. That split matches after and is not an attribution error.
